title: Surrey Heath Borough Council: learning and collaborating on AI
summary: Surrey Heath reports promising meeting-recap and email-summary tests with two Copilot licenses. It has not established a business case or quantified gains.
account: Surrey Heath used two Copilot licenses to test meeting recaps, email summaries, policy drafts, and presentations. The council describes useful early results and seeks a stronger business case. Time savings, financial returns, and benefits from wider deployment remain unmeasured.
purpose: Explore practical AI uses and identify whether a small council can establish a worthwhile business case.
domain: Local-government administration and exploratory AI adoption

ratings.reason: The council describes useful meeting recaps and long-email summaries in its initial tests. Time and cost savings are unquantified.

ai_role.statement: Two senior IT users tested meeting recaps, email summaries, drafting, and presentations. The source reports promising task convenience, but it does not quantify realized savings or establish a wider deployment benefit.

evidence.citation: Council or project account published in the Local Government Association AI case-study bank. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Surrey Heath Borough Council: learning and collaborating on AI

produced_by: The exploratory phase used two Copilot licenses allocated to senior IT staff.
The council focused on a limited set of low-risk administrative uses while considering training and organizational readiness.
must_hold: The conditions needed to reproduce the benefit are unspecified.

headline: Surrey Heath explores Copilot meeting and email summaries
claim_basis: Sources: the deployer's report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
